what_happened_next.text:
Netflix and the US share basket more than doubled over five years. Amazon nearly doubled, but Disney finished only slightly higher. The bond estimate fell a little. This starting date came after a sharp market fall, so it gives a different picture from buying before the outbreak.

The pandemic was already known when you invested. Later that year, WHO listed its first COVID-19 vaccine for emergency use. In 2022, the Fed began raising interest rates, and Webb released a full set of scientific images. The situation continued to change long after the urgent first headlines.

Disney’s small final gain is useful beside the much larger gains elsewhere. Getting back above the starting amount is different from growing quickly. Bonds also show that a government-loan investment can lose market value. You could not know these exact paths in March 2020. A plan made then had to allow for several futures, including a slower recovery or a different set of winning companies.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: The pandemic had closed venues and changed daily life. Companies hired workers, adjusted services and tried to cope with sudden demand changes.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The starting price mattered as well as the company. Gains measured from this month do not erase losses suffered by someone who bought earlier.
reflection.what_faded_away: A hiring plan or busy streaming service did not translate into a guaranteed stock return. Business activity and share prices are connected, but not identical.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The length of the disruption, the recovery and later interest rates were uncertain. The final chart leaves out how hard it felt to make choices then.

hot_stock_outcomes.text: Disney began near the pandemic shock, with parks closing and movies disrupted. Its parks later recovered, and entertainment streaming moved from a $2.5 billion annual loss in fiscal 2023 to a small profit in 2024. Inside Out 2 was another bright spot, but traditional TV kept shrinking. Those improvements and problems pulled in different directions, leaving only a small overall gain from March 2020.

Online shopping surged during the pandemic: Amazon’s sales rose 40% in the quarter ended June 2020. Over the following years, cloud computing and a more efficient delivery network helped turn growth into much bigger profits. In 2024, Amazon earned $59.2 billion, nearly twice its 2023 profit. AWS alone produced $39.8 billion in profit from running the business, showing why Amazon’s business was about more than shopping.

Netflix found new ways to earn money from its audience. It launched a cheaper plan with advertisements in November 2022, then expanded charges for sharing accounts outside a household in 2023. By the end of 2024, it had over 300 million paid memberships. Annual revenue grew 16% and profit from running the business passed $10 billion, giving the stock’s rise support from stronger business results.
